concepts.why: The presence of a systolic murmur, a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt, and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior and inferior vena cava to the right atrium support the diagnosis of an atrial septal defect.
The ECG findings of a complete right bundle-branch block with a normal PR interval support the diagnosis of a right bundle-branch block.
The ECG findings of a fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads support the diagnosis of a fragmented QRS.
The absence of symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, and lower limb swelling, along with normal vital parameters, support the diagnosis of a normal pregnancy.

The presence of a dilated right atrium and ventricle, along with a large defect, may also suggest the possibility of a ventricular septal defect, although the primary diagnosis is an atrial septal defect.
The echocardiogram finding of a dilated right atrium supports the diagnosis of right atrial enlargement.
The echocardiogram finding of a dilated right ventricle supports the diagnosis of right ventricular enlargement.
The presence of a large defect with a left-to-right shunt and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior and inferior vena cava to the right atrium supports the diagnosis of a left-to-right shunt.
